content: 1. Benzodiazepines that undergo oxidative metabolism may have increased serum concentrations when co-administered with other benzodiazepines due to reduced clearance. This can lead to prolonged sedative effects. Monitoring is recommended. 2. Ethinylestradiol can increase the systemic exposure of intranasal midazolam by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, potentially prolonging sedation. Caution and monitoring are advised. 3. Mifepristone reduces the effects of ethinylestradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Backup contraceptive methods are recommended, and close monitoring is necessary. 4. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 5. Mitotane decreases the levels of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of cytochrome P450 3A4, and dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. Monitoring is recommended. 6. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of ethinylestradiol by competing for plasma protein binding. As a BCRP inhibitor, momelotinib may increase the exposure of BCRP substrates, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 7. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Nafcillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 9. Nemolizumab decreases the levels of norelgesteromin and ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nemolizumab suppresses cytokines, which may increase CYP enzyme activity. Monitoring for decreased systemic levels of sensitive CYP substrates is necessary, and dosage modifications may be required. 10. Neomycin (oral) decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, which is downregulated during infection and inflammation. Caution is advised when co-administering with CYP substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. 12. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 13. Ethinylestradiol may increase the plasma concentrations and adverse effects of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) such as amitriptyline, amoxapine, desipramine, doxepin, imipramine, nortriptyline, protriptyline, and trimipramine by reducing their oxidative metabolism. Monitoring is advised due to the potential for increased TCA-related adverse effects. 14. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 15. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of antipyrine, asenapine, duloxetine, and ramelteon by inhibiting hepatic enzymes such as CYP1A2 and CYP3A4. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 16. Rosuvastatin increases the levels of ethinylestradiol through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib (oral and topical) and tizanidine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. 18. Ethinylestradiol increases the effects of naratriptan through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Nefazodone increases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 20. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels of bendamustine by inhibiting its metabolism via CYP1A2. Bendamustine is metabolized to minimally active metabolites. Monitoring is recommended. 21. Ethinylestradiol decreases the effects of albiglutide by impairing glucose tolerance, potentially reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitoring glycemic control in diabetic patients is advised. 22. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of alosetron and alprazolam by inhibiting their metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 23. Ethinylestradiol may increase hypercoagulability when used with aminocaproic acid due to additive effects on clotting factor production and fibrinolysis inhibition. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 25. Amoxicillin and ampicillin decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 27. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 28. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is recommended. 29. Atazanavir may increase or decrease the levels of norelgesteromin and ethinylestradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 30. Ethinylestradiol increases the levels or effects of atogepant, atorvastatin, and axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism or affecting P-glycoprotein transport. Monitoring is recommended. 31. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Belzutifan may also cause fetal harm based on animal studies.
